opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: The main applicant must have BES membership. Groups must have a diverse mix of members at different career stages, institutions and international participation.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing up to £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups of 8-15 individuals who analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for a decade of data collection; first five years' funding (£3,500) claimable in year 1, with an additional £3,500 in year 6.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers and consultants, as well as university academics. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level, in formal or informal educational settings. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Improving the education of future generations of ecologists by providing up to £5k towards evidence-based learning, funding research on teaching and learning practices within ecology.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants

amount.raw: Grant awards of up to £20,000 can be claimed from the applicant.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations. Undergraduates and masters students not eligible. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Promoting interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements in different disciplines and sectors, immersing an ecologist in another professional world for up to 12 months.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Funding provided for researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Member-only grant scheme. Not a scholarship; cannot fund completion of an undergraduate or master's degree or part of a funded fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Providing up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: The lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels. No restrictions on where applicants come from or where they carry out outreach work.
opportunities.summary: Providing funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £250 is available to cover registration fees for virtual conferences/courses; a maximum of £500 is available for events in person.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (PGR) registered on a postgraduate research degree programme. Postdoc researchers, undergraduates and masters students not eligible. Must work/study at a university or research institution.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and the travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences. Round 3 opens 24 August 2026.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage, a citizen of and based in a Global South country, travelling from and returning to that country, and must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting. Must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering costs such as registration, transport, food and accommodation. Open call 17 July 2026 - 8 September 2026.
